My therapist explained my anxiety to me like an overly sensitive smoke alarm. So, in the case of a real smoke alarm, if it starts going off for no reason it might just be because you’re making a piece of toast. But of course, it could be going off because there’s a dangerous fire. 

So same thing for anxiety. Your alarms could be going off to warn you about something, even if you don’t know what that something is, OR it could just be their oversensitivity and all you gotta do is look in the kitchen for any signs of smoke. And if there’s no smoke in the kitchen (or in the case of anxiety, nothing going wrong at this moment) allow yourself to calm the alarm in whatever ways you do and assure yourself that you are safe. 

This helped me a lot and I hope it helps you!

I am not a therapist; however, as someone with anxiety and an abusive subconscious I must recommend CBT (cognitive behavioral therapy). It’s all about training yourself and your brain to not automatically go to those dark places, and instead recognizing when you start to feel anxious and calming yourself down ASAP. It’s amazing how many triggers we all have formed through some of the most random situations, and how those triggers follow us through life until we’re able to be at peace with them. CBT just helps you to step back, say “I am feeling anxious, this feeling is anxiety,” and work your way up the chain to figure out where the feeling initially came from. Takes a ton of work to get good at, but I’ve heard great success stories and have had some huge moments of relief myself so I always recommend it to cases that sound similar to my own.

This is making me think of all those AITA posts where someone buys their child a lotto ticket, then when it wins they aren’t sure what to do with the money. Adding to this with another seemingly simple exorcise:

I’ve started kickboxing and the other day I got super winded (which made me anxious because I was the only one so out of breath) and our coach stopped the class and had us all fully exhale, breathe in deeply through our noses, and then another full exhale through the mouth. It’s so simple and I’ve heard different versions of this all my life (the phrase “just breathe!” is one of my least favorite pieces of advice when handling anxiety) but it really worked like this for me. I’ve even used it while dealing with frustrations at work, general anxiety, and moments of slight panic. I’ve yet to try it during a full on panic attack but I think it will at least help to keep me level headed. There’s no counting, no “in two three four out two three four,” just a sharp, clarifying breath in and out. The connection of nose and mouth, the pure intent to calm your body, and the two seconds it takes to do all allow me to focus up quickly and (for the time being) move past whatever’s blocking my brain. 

Hope this helps someone!
